title: Compare streamed exact-quota external shuffle adapters
question: Do one-pass output pipes improve the chosen external comparator workflows while preserving full fields and exact quotas?
summary: At 2 GiB qsvlite piping reduces elapsed 6.25% and GNU time filesystem outputs 60.44% with 20.19% more CPU. Native DuckDB COPY piped to qsvlite split reduces complete elapsed 45.27% versus the materialized DuckDB adapter.

workloads: 2 GiB plain fixed-width CSV, exact 8 parts, 1 GiB hard cgroup without swap, one requested worker per command.

validation.summary: Two opposite-order full job pairs per workflow. Complete exact field, unique ID, quota, size and nonidentity oracle. Small preflights and prior failed alternatives preserved.

limitations: WSL2/ext4, fixed-width line-safe divisible fixture. Tool pipelines can use overlapping processes even with one worker requested per command.
The faster DuckDB workflow uses qsvlite for final split. GNU time file counters and cgroup refaults do not identify logical managed bytes or complete device traffic.
exclusions: Small flights and unsuccessful implicit stdin, extensionless split and partitioned DuckDB COPY attempts. Verification and fixture identity outside timed command.
reopen_when: Qualify full 40 GiB streams under the same hard cap to check viability and whether the 2 GiB traffic savings transfer.
